title: Stage 1: Hello, HTTP
summary: Start a web server and answer your first two requests.

steps.title: What you are building
body: Over this project you will build the back end of a task tracker: a **REST API** that a web page or a phone app could talk to. It will list tasks, create them, update them, validate input, and protect itself with an API key.
You write a real `Program.cs`. The dojo starts it as a real web server on your machine and its tests call it over real HTTP, exactly as a browser would.
Your code carries forward: each stage starts from what you finished in the stage before.
- `builder` is where you configure the app before it exists (services, settings).
- `app.MapGet("/hello", ...)` says: *when a GET request arrives for `/hello`, run this lambda and send back what it returns*. That pairing of a URL and a handler is an **endpoint**.
- `app.Run()` starts the server and blocks, listening for requests until the program is stopped. It is always the last line.

steps.prompt: Arrange the lines into a working web app with one endpoint.
steps.explain: Configure, build, map the endpoints, run. Anything after `app.Run()` would not execute until the server shuts down.

steps.title: A health check
prompt: Almost every real API has a health endpoint that monitoring tools call to ask *are you alive?*
Add an endpoint so that `GET /health` responds with the text `ok`.
Press **Run checks**: the dojo starts your server and calls it.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
Dojo.Eq("GET /health returns the text ok", "ok", await DojoWeb.Text(r));
DojoWeb.Status("GET /nothing-here responds 404 Not Found", 404, await http.GetAsync("/nothing-here"));
hints: The handler can be a lambda with no parameters that returns a string: `() => "ok"`.

steps.title: Returning JSON
body: Returning a `string` sends plain text. Return **an object** and ASP.NET Core turns it into JSON for you.
A record works just as well, and gives the shape a name you can reuse:
Property names are written in **camelCase** in the JSON (`zone`, `hour`), which is the convention on the web. Type declarations such as records go at the bottom of the file, after `app.Run()`.

steps.explain: Objects are serialized to JSON with camelCase property names. The third option is what `ToString()` gives a record, which is not what goes over the wire.

steps.title: Describe the service
prompt: Keep `/health`. Add `GET /` so that the root of the API describes itself as JSON:
`version` must be a number, not a string.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
Dojo.Eq("GET /health still returns ok", "ok", await DojoWeb.Text(await http.GetAsync("/health")));
Dojo.Check("GET / responds with JSON", r.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType == "application/json", "the content type was " + r.Content.Headers.ContentType);
hints: Return an object, not a string, and it becomes JSON.
An anonymous object is enough: `new { name = "Tasks API", version = 1 }`.
